es: Sin coma entre verbo y su complemento
en: No comma between a verb and its object

es: Regla de oro: NADA entre el verbo y su "that". Si dudas, lee sin la coma — si fluye, no la pongas.
en: Golden rule: NOTHING between a verb and its “that”. If in doubt, read it without the comma — if it flows, leave it out.

es: Coma entre el verbo y "that" → corta el verbo de su objeto.
en: A comma between the verb and “that” → it cuts the verb off from its object.

es: El punto convierte "Although… flood." en un fragmento sin verbo principal.
en: The period turns “Although… flood.” into a fragment with no main verb.

es: “it” y “the largest of any bird alive today” indican UNA ave (singular). El wingspan le pertenece → posesivo singular = nombre + ’s: “the albatross’s wingspan”.
en: “it” and “the largest of any bird alive today” indicate ONE bird (singular). The wingspan belongs to it → singular possessive = noun + ’s: “the albatross’s wingspan”.

es: Sin la coma de apertura, el inciso cierra pero no abre → desbalanceado.
en: Without the opening comma, the aside closes but never opens → unbalanced.

es: Falta la coma antes de “but”; sin ella, unir dos oraciones completas es incorrecto en el SAT.
en: The comma before “but” is missing; without it, joining two complete sentences is wrong on the SAT.

es: El colon no cierra un inciso abierto con raya.
en: A colon does not close an aside that was opened with a dash.

es: Plural sin posesivo, y contradice el singular “it”.
en: A plural with no possessive, and it contradicts the singular “it”.

es: La coma entre “who… Beethoven” y su verbo “was” separa el sujeto de su verbo.
en: The comma between “who… Beethoven” and its verb “was” separates the subject from its verb.

es: Falta el punto y coma antes de “however”.
en: The semicolon before “however” is missing.

es: “Far from ___ing” invierte el sentido esperado. Si crece el conflicto (“sharper, more entrenched”), busca un verbo de INTENSIFICAR, no de calmar ni aplazar.
en: “Far from ___ing” flips the expected meaning. If the conflict grows (“sharper, more entrenched”), look for a verb meaning to INTENSIFY, not to calm or postpone.

es: “Derivative” (copiado de otros) no viene al caso; nada dice que imite otras obras.
en: “Derivative” is beside the point; nothing says it imitates other works.

es: “Candor” (franqueza, honestidad) es un rasgo moral que el texto no menciona.
en: “Candor” is a moral trait the text never mentions.

es: “Tedious” (aburrido) juzga el estilo, pero el texto habla de SESGO, no de si aburren.
en: “Tedious” judges the style, but the text is about BIAS, not about whether they are boring.

es: “Transparent” (claro, honesto) es lo contrario de lo que describe el texto: oculta costos y no verifica nada.
en: “Transparent” is the opposite of what the text describes: it hides costs and verifies nothing.

es: “For example” anuncia un ejemplo de algo dicho antes, pero la 2ª idea no ejemplifica a la 1ª, la sigue en el tiempo.
en: “For example” announces an example of something said before, but the 2nd idea does not exemplify the 1st, it follows it in time.

es: “For instance” introduce un ejemplo, pero el deslizamiento no es un ejemplo de la lluvia, es su efecto.
en: “For instance” introduces an example, but the landslide is not an example of the rain, it is its effect.

es: No compara amenazas urbanas contra rurales; el foco es el valor de los techos, no un peligro exclusivo de la ciudad.
en: It does not compare urban threats against rural ones; the focus is the value of the roofs, not a danger exclusive to the city.

es: Falta la coma de cierre tras floor; el apositivo se abre pero no se cierra, y se pega a and.
en: The closing comma after floor is missing; the appositive opens but never closes, and it runs straight into and.

es: Subraya un parecido (ambos se queman), no el contraste que pide la meta.
en: It underlines a similarity (both burn), not the contrast the goal calls for.

es: El sujeto es “The collection” (singular). La frase “of rare beetles that the museum acquired…” solo describe al sujeto y no lo cambia. Un sujeto singular pide un verbo singular: “includes”.
en: The subject is “The collection” (singular). The phrase “of rare beetles that the museum acquired…” only describes the subject and does not change it. A singular subject calls for a singular verb: “includes”.

es: “has destroyed” es presente perfecto; no encaja con el marco claramente pasado “arrived”.
en: “has destroyed” is present perfect; it does not fit the clearly past frame “arrived”.

es: “is destroying” es presente continuo; choca con el pasado “arrived”.
en: “is destroying” is present continuous; it clashes with the past “arrived”.

es: “submits” es presente; rompe con el pasado “reviewed”.
en: “submits” is present tense; it breaks with the past “reviewed”.

es: “our” es primera persona; el texto habla de los investigadores en tercera persona, no de nosotros.
en: “our” is first person; the text speaks about the researchers in the third person, not about us.

es: “their” es plural, pero el ritmo pertenece a un solo libro (singular).
en: “their” is plural, but the pacing belongs to a single book (singular).

es: Solo habla de la levadura comercial; no menciona el sourdough para comparar.
en: It only talks about commercial yeast; it never mentions sourdough to compare.

es: Solo describe el podcast; falta el lado de la radio para comparar.
en: It only describes the podcast; the radio side is missing for the comparison.

es: Describe el punto bajo, pero no muestra el crecimiento posterior.
en: It describes the low point, but does not show the growth that followed.

es: Contrasta el AHORRO (40% vs. 38%), justo lo que la meta pide no enfatizar.
en: It contrasts the SAVINGS (40% vs. 38%), exactly what the goal tells you not to emphasize.

es: Descuento de p% → multiplica por (1 \u2212 p/100) en un solo paso. "Reduced by 35%" = \u00d70.65. Nunca calcules el descuento aparte si piden el precio final.
en: A discount of p% → multiply by (1 \u2212 p/100) in one step. “Reduced by 35%” = \u00d70.65. Never compute the discount separately when they want the final price.

es: Usa y = mx + b con m = −2 y el punto (3, 4): 4 = −2(3) + b → 4 = −6 + b → b = 10. La recta es y = −2x + 10. (Comprueba: −2(3)+10 = 4 ✓.)
en: Use y = mx + b with m = −2 and the point (3, 4): 4 = −2(3) + b → 4 = −6 + b → b = 10. The line is y = −2x + 10. (Check: −2(3)+10 = 4 ✓.)

es: Resuelve el sistema. De x + y = 7 → x = 7 − y. Sustituye: 2(7 − y) + 3y = 18 → 14 − 2y + 3y = 18 → 14 + y = 18 → y = 4. Entonces x = 7 − 4 = 3. Piden x + 2y = 3 + 2(4) = 3 + 8 = 11. (Comprueba el sistema: 2(3)+3(4) = 18 ✓ y 3+4 = 7 ✓.) Respuesta: 11.
en: Solve the system. From x + y = 7 → x = 7 − y. Substitute: 2(7 − y) + 3y = 18 → 14 − 2y + 3y = 18 → 14 + y = 18 → y = 4. Then x = 7 − 4 = 3. They want x + 2y = 3 + 2(4) = 3 + 8 = 11. (Check the system: 2(3)+3(4) = 18 ✓ and 3+4 = 7 ✓.) Answer: 11.

es: Pendiente = subida/avance = Δy/Δx. Resta en el MISMO orden arriba y abajo: (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁). Nunca dejes el Δy solo.
en: Slope = rise/run = Δy/Δx. Subtract in the SAME order on top and bottom: (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁). Never leave the Δy on its own.

es: Traduce: "fijo" = constante, "por hora" = coeficiente de h. Arma total = fijo + tarifa×h, luego resta el fijo ANTES de dividir.
en: Translate it: “flat” = the constant, “per hour” = the coefficient of h. Build total = flat + rate×h, then subtract the flat fee BEFORE dividing.

es: 3 es el cambio en x (4 − 1), no la pendiente. Es el denominador, no el resultado.
en: 3 is the change in x (4 − 1), not the slope. It is the denominator, not the result.

es: 6 es 2x sin restar el 5, o un despeje incompleto de y.
en: 6 is 2x without subtracting the 5, or an incomplete solve for y.

es: x ≤ −2 invierte el signo (bien) pero calcula −6/−3 = 2, no −2. El resultado es +2.
en: x ≤ −2 flips the sign (correctly) but computes −6/−3 = 2, not −2. The result is +2.

es: Truco Desmos: grafica y = x² y y = x + 6, toca los dos puntos de corte: (−2, 4) y (3, 9). Ojo: piden el mayor VALOR DE y (9), no el mayor valor de x.
en: Desmos trick: graph y = x² and y = x + 6, and tap the two intersection points: (−2, 4) and (3, 9). Careful: they want the greatest VALUE OF y (9), not the greatest value of x.

es: Porcentaje de cambio = (nuevo − viejo) / VIEJO. El denominador siempre es el valor de partida. Divide entre 75 y ya te equivocaste.
en: Percent change = (new − old) / OLD. The denominator is always the starting value. Divide by 75 and you have already gone wrong.

es: 245 es el 70% de 350; no corresponde al 40% que se pide.
en: 245 is 70% of 350; it does not match the 40% being asked for.

es: Dos trampas fijas: (1) los signos se INVIERTEN respecto al centro — centro (2, −3) da (x − 2) y (y + 3). (2) el lado derecho es r², no r. Radio 5 → 25.
en: Two fixed traps: (1) the signs FLIP relative to the center — center (2, −3) gives (x − 2) and (y + 3). (2) the right-hand side is r², not r. Radius 5 → 25.

es: 6π usa el radio (6) como si fuera la circunferencia, olvidando el 2πr. 6 es solo el radio.
en: 6π uses the radius (6) as if it were the circumference, forgetting the 2πr. 6 is only the radius.

es: 3/5 es sin θ (opuesto/hipotenusa = 6/10). Te pidieron el coseno, que usa el cateto ADYACENTE.
en: 3/5 is sin θ (opposite/hypotenuse = 6/10). They asked for the cosine, which uses the ADJACENT leg.

es: “Novel” casi nunca significa “novela” en el SAT. La pista “no laboratory had tried before” apunta a “nuevo/innovador”, no a “complicado”.
en: “Novel” almost never means “a novel” on the SAT. The clue “no laboratory had tried before” points to “new/innovative”, not to “complicated”.

es: “Rather than rigid commands” pide lo contrario de imponer. Predice “abiertas, propuestas con suavidad”: esa es “tentative”.
en: “Rather than rigid commands” calls for the opposite of imposing. Predict “open, gently proposed”: that is “tentative”.

es: “Abundant” (abundante) contradice el desierto, donde llueve poco y hay pocas plantas.
en: “Abundant” contradicts the desert, where rain is scarce and plants are few.

es: “Colorful” (colorido) no se relaciona con la pista: el texto habla de sobrevivir sin agua, no de colores.
en: “Colorful” has nothing to do with the clue: the text is about surviving without water, not about color.

es: “Interview” (entrevistar) no encaja: no se opone a mostrar sus defectos; el contraste es con “polished statue”.
en: “Interview” does not fit: it does not oppose showing his flaws; the contrast is with “polished statue”.

es: “Criticize” (criticar) es lo contrario del punto: ella no lo ataca, solo se niega a idealizarlo.
en: “Criticize” is the opposite of the point: she does not attack him, she just refuses to idealize him.

es: “Therefore” marca consecuencia, y sembrar flores no es un efecto de haber cultivado solo vegetales, es un giro contra esa costumbre.
en: “Therefore” marks consequence, and planting flowers is not an effect of having grown only vegetables, it is a turn against that habit.

es: Regla de oro: NADA entre el verbo y su "that". Si dudas, lee sin la coma — si fluye, no la pongas.
en: Golden rule: NOTHING between a verb and its “that”. If in doubt, read it without the comma — if it flows, leave it out.

es: Dos oraciones completas seguidas necesitan algo: ";", ".", o coma + FANBOYS. Nunca una coma sola ni nada.
en: Two complete sentences back to back need something: “;”, “.”, or a comma + FANBOYS. Never a lone comma and never nothing.

es: Falta la coma antes de "but"; sin ella, unir dos oraciones completas es incorrecto en el SAT.
en: The comma before “but” is missing; without it, joining two complete sentences is wrong on the SAT.

es: Sin la coma de apertura, el inciso cierra pero no abre → desbalanceado.
en: Without the opening comma, the aside closes but never opens → unbalanced.

es: El colon no cierra un inciso abierto con raya.
en: A colon does not close an aside that was opened with a dash.

es: Coma entre el verbo "concluded" y "that" → separa el verbo de su objeto.
en: A comma between the verb “concluded” and “that” → it separates the verb from its object.

es: Falta el punto y coma antes de "therefore".
en: The semicolon before “therefore” is missing.

es: "so" sin la coma antes no basta para unir dos oraciones completas en el SAT.
en: “so” with no comma before it is not enough to join two complete sentences on the SAT.

es: Cuenta que era inventora autodidacta; no muestra el efecto duradero de su idea.
en: It tells us she was a self-taught inventor; it does not show the lasting effect of her idea.

es: Usa y = mx + b con m = 3 y el punto (2, 1): 1 = 3(2) + b → 1 = 6 + b → b = −5. La recta es y = 3x − 5. (Comprueba: 3(2)−5 = 1 ✓.)
en: Use y = mx + b with m = 3 and the point (2, 1): 1 = 3(2) + b → 1 = 6 + b → b = −5. The line is y = 3x − 5. (Check: 3(2)−5 = 1 ✓.)

es: 3 es el valor de y, no de x. La pregunta pide x — no confundas las variables.
en: 3 is the value of y, not of x. The question asks for x — do not mix up the variables.

es: (0, −4) usa la pendiente (−4) como si fuera el intercepto. La pendiente es m, no b.
en: (0, −4) uses the slope (−4) as if it were the intercept. The slope is m, not b.

es: 8 es el valor de y, no de x. La pregunta pide x — no confundas las variables.
en: 8 is the value of y, not of x. The question asks for x — do not mix up the variables.

es: 2 sale de olvidar el −4 al sustituir: 5x = 16 → no; falta sumar 4 antes de dividir.
en: 2 comes from forgetting the −4 when substituting: 5x = 16 → no; you have to add 4 before dividing.

es: 3 es el precio de la soda (s), no del hot dog. La pregunta pide el hot dog.
en: 3 is the price of the soda (s), not the hot dog. The question asks for the hot dog.

es: 5 es el costo total de 1 hot dog + 1 soda, no el precio del hot dog solo.
en: 5 is the combined cost of 1 hot dog + 1 soda, not the price of the hot dog alone.

es: x ≤ 3 ni invierte la desigualdad ni maneja bien el signo del 3.
en: x ≤ 3 neither flips the inequality nor handles the sign of the 3 correctly.

es: $13.00 es el costo total del viaje de 4 millas, no el cargo fijo. Incluye el millaje.
en: $13.00 is the total cost of the 4-mile trip, not the fixed charge. It includes the mileage.

es: 168 es 12 × 14, el paso intermedio. Falta dividir entre 7.
en: 168 is 12 × 14, the intermediate step. You still have to divide by 7.

es: 14 es 7x, el resultado de la resta antes de despejar. Falta dividir entre 7.
en: 14 is 7x, the result of the subtraction before solving. You still have to divide by 7.

es: Media (hallar el dato que falta)
en: Mean (finding the missing value)

es: Pendiente = (10 − (−2))/(5 − 1) = 12/4 = 3. Ojo con el numerador: restar −2 SUMA 2.
en: Slope = (10 − (−2))/(5 − 1) = 12/4 = 3. Watch the numerator: subtracting −2 ADDS 2.

es: f(−2) = (−2)² − 3(−2) = 4 − (−6) = 4 + 6 = 10. Los dos signos importan: el cuadrado de un negativo es positivo, y restar −6 suma.
en: f(−2) = (−2)² − 3(−2) = 4 − (−6) = 4 + 6 = 10. Both signs matter: the square of a negative is positive, and subtracting −6 adds.

es: Descontar 25 % es pagar el 75 %: 0.75 × 80 = $60. (O bien: el descuento es 0.25 × 80 = $20, y 80 − 20 = $60.)
en: Taking 25% off means paying 75%: 0.75 × 80 = $60. (Or: the discount is 0.25 × 80 = $20, and 80 − 20 = $60.)

es: 20 es solo 5(4): falta sumar el 2.
en: 20 is only 5(4): you forgot to add the 2.

es: −3 tiene el signo cambiado. Si y sube de −2 a 10 mientras x crece, la pendiente es positiva.
en: −3 has the sign flipped. If y rises from −2 to 10 as x grows, the slope is positive.

es: 16 es 2x, el paso intermedio. Falta dividir entre 2.
en: 16 is 2x, the intermediate step. You still have to divide by 2.

es: 8 es el valor de −b, sin dividir entre 2a.
en: 8 is the value of −b, without dividing by 2a.

es: Pone la coma en el lugar equivocado, separando «a salamander» de su propio modificador y dejando igual sin cerrar el aposito.
en: It puts the comma in the wrong place, separating “a salamander” from its own modifier and still leaving the appositive unclosed.

es: Porcentaje de cambio = (nuevo − viejo) / VIEJO. El denominador siempre es el valor de partida (45), no el nuevo.
en: Percent change = (new − old) / OLD. The denominator is always the starting value (45), not the new one.

es: 16 es la media aproximada (114/7 ≈ 16.3), no la mediana. La mediana es el valor del medio, no el promedio.
en: 16 is roughly the mean (114/7 ≈ 16.3), not the median. The median is the middle value, not the average.

es: 22 es el punto medio entre el menor (8) y el mayor (30); eso no es la mediana.
en: 22 is the midpoint between the smallest (8) and the largest (30); that is not the median.

es: Completa cuadrados. En x: x² − 10x = (x − 5)² − 25. En y: y² + 4y = (y + 2)² − 4. Queda (x − 5)² + (y + 2)² − 25 − 4 + 13 = 0 → (x − 5)² + (y + 2)² = 16. El centro es (5, −2).
en: Complete the square. In x: x² − 10x = (x − 5)² − 25. In y: y² + 4y = (y + 2)² − 4. That leaves (x − 5)² + (y + 2)² − 25 − 4 + 13 = 0 → (x − 5)² + (y + 2)² = 16. The center is (5, −2).

es: El radio es la distancia del centro (1, 2) al punto (5, 5). Distancia = √((5−1)² + (5−2)²) = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5.
en: The radius is the distance from the center (1, 2) to the point (5, 5). Distance = √((5−1)² + (5−2)²) = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5.

es: In a right triangle the two acute angles are complementary (A + B = 90°). For complementary angles, sin A = cos B. That is why cos B = sin A = 0.6. (The side opposite A is the side adjacent to B, so both ratios use the same side over the hypotenuse.)
en: In a right triangle the two acute angles are complementary (A + B = 90°). For complementary angles, sin A = cos B. That is why cos B = sin A = 0.6. (The side opposite A is the side adjacent to B, so both ratios use the same side over the hypotenuse.)

es: 16π eleva la altura (4²=16) en vez del radio. Se eleva el RADIO al cuadrado, no la altura.
en: 16π squares the height (4²=16) instead of the radius. It is the RADIUS that gets squared, not the height.

es: 0.8 es cos A (usando sin²A + cos²A = 1: cos A = √(1−0.36) = 0.8), pero te piden cos B, no cos A. Y cos B = sin A = 0.6.
en: 0.8 is cos A (using sin²A + cos²A = 1: cos A = √(1−0.36) = 0.8), but they want cos B, not cos A. And cos B = sin A = 0.6.

es: El antecedente es “A person” (singular, tercera persona). El pronombre reflexivo singular que le corresponde es “himself or herself”.
en: The antecedent is “A person” (singular, third person). The matching singular reflexive pronoun is “himself or herself”.

es: Un sustantivo colectivo tratado como unidad (“The orchestra”) pide el posesivo singular “its”.
en: A collective noun treated as a unit (“The orchestra”) calls for the singular possessive “its”.

es: “they” es plural; no concuerda con el antecedente singular “a student”.
en: “they” is plural; it does not agree with the singular antecedent “a student”.

es: “we” es primera persona; el texto habla del estudiante en tercera persona, no de nosotros.
en: “we” is first person; the text speaks about the student in the third person, not about us.

es: “their” es plural; no concuerda con el singular “Any hiker”.
en: “their” is plural; it does not agree with the singular “Any hiker”.

es: “themselves” es plural; no concuerda con el singular “A person”.
en: “themselves” is plural; it does not agree with the singular “A person”.

es: “ourselves” es primera persona plural; no encaja con el singular en tercera persona “A person”.
en: “ourselves” is first person plural; it does not fit the third-person singular “A person”.

es: “whomever” es caso objeto; el pronombre hace de sujeto del verbo “has shown”, no de objeto.
en: “whomever” is the object case; the pronoun serves as the subject of the verb “has shown”, not as an object.

es: El sujeto es “Each of the volunteers”, y “each” es singular. El pronombre posesivo singular que concuerda es “his or her”: “bring his or her own gloves”.
en: The subject is “Each of the volunteers”, and “each” is singular. The matching singular possessive pronoun is “his or her”: “bring his or her own gloves”.

es: El sujeto es “The collection” (singular); “of rare butterfly specimens… expeditions” es solo un modificador. El verbo singular en presente que concuerda es “is”: “The collection… is now displayed”.
en: The subject is “The collection” (singular); “of rare butterfly specimens… expeditions” is only a modifier. The singular present-tense verb that agrees is “is”: “The collection… is now displayed”.

es: “Their” es plural; no concuerda con el sujeto singular “each”.
en: “Their” is plural; it does not agree with the singular subject “each”.

es: “Have been” es plural; no concuerda con el sujeto singular “collection”.
en: “Have been” is plural; it does not agree with the singular subject “collection”.

es: Da un dato menor (el horario de las clases) en lugar de resumir el impacto general.
en: It gives a minor fact (the class schedule) instead of summing up the overall impact.

es: Resta 2: 5x = 2. Divide entre 5: x = 2/5 = 0.4. (Verifica: 5(2/5) + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4 ✓.) En el box valen 2/5, .4 o 0.4.
en: Subtract 2: 5x = 2. Divide by 5: x = 2/5 = 0.4. (Check: 5(2/5) + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4 ✓.) The box accepts 2/5, .4 or 0.4.

es: No escribas el paso intermedio (12): termina de despejar hasta el final antes de llenar el box.
en: Do not write the intermediate step (12): finish solving before you fill the box.

es: Descuentos: calcula el total, aplica el porcentaje y resta (o multiplica directo por 0.80). Nunca escribas $ ni unidades en el grid.
en: Discounts: compute the total, apply the percentage and subtract (or multiply straight by 0.80). Never write $ or units in the grid.

es: Use cos(2θ) = 1 − 2sin²(θ), which depends only on sin²(θ): cos(2θ) = 1 − 2(9/25) = 1 − 18/25 = 7/25. Verification another way: in Q2, cos(θ) = −4/5, and cos²θ − sin²θ = 16/25 − 9/25 = 7/25 ✓. Even though θ is in the second quadrant, cos(2θ) comes out positive.
en: Use cos(2θ) = 1 − 2sin²(θ), which depends only on sin²(θ): cos(2θ) = 1 − 2(9/25) = 1 − 18/25 = 7/25. Verification another way: in Q2, cos(θ) = −4/5, and cos²θ − sin²θ = 16/25 − 9/25 = 7/25 ✓. Even though θ is in the second quadrant, cos(2θ) comes out positive.

es: Double angle: cos(2θ) = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin²θ. Pick the form that uses the data you have (here only sin θ) and mind the sign of cos θ by quadrant if you need it.
en: Double angle: cos(2θ) = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin²θ. Pick the form that uses the data you have (here only sin θ) and mind the sign of cos θ by quadrant if you need it.

es: 2 es solo f(−1), el paso interno; falta aplicar f una segunda vez.
en: 2 is only f(−1), the inner step; you still have to apply f a second time.

es: 35/84 sobrecuenta los favorables; el conteo correcto es C(5,2) × C(3,1) = 30.
en: 35/84 overcounts the favorable cases; the correct count is C(5,2) × C(3,1) = 30.

es: 40/84 sobrecuenta (10 × 4 usa 4 azules, pero solo hay 3: C(3,1) = 3).
en: 40/84 overcounts (10 × 4 uses 4 blue ones, but there are only 3: C(3,1) = 3).

es: “have been” es plural; no concuerda con el sujeto singular “collection”.
en: “have been” is plural; it does not agree with the singular subject “collection”.

es: Sin nada, las dos oraciones se fusionan en un run-on (“…stress test the engineers refused…”).
en: With nothing there, the two sentences fuse into a run-on (“…stress test the engineers refused…”).

es: 3 es el valor de y, no de x. Sumando bien las ecuaciones, x = 4.
en: 3 is the value of y, not of x. Adding the equations correctly gives x = 4.

es: 7 es x + y (4 + 3), no x sola. Te pidieron solo el valor de x.
en: 7 is x + y (4 + 3), not x alone. They asked only for the value of x.

es: Dos soluciones es imposible en un sistema de dos rectas: o se cruzan una vez, o nunca, o coinciden en infinitos puntos.
en: Two solutions is impossible for a system of two lines: they either cross once, never, or coincide at infinitely many points.

es: Completa cuadrados. En x: x² + 10x = (x + 5)² − 25. En y: y² − 4y = (y − 2)² − 4. Sustituyendo: (x + 5)² − 25 + (y − 2)² − 4 − 7 = 0 → (x + 5)² + (y − 2)² = 36. El centro es (h, k) = (−5, 2) y el radio es 6.
en: Complete the square. In x: x² + 10x = (x + 5)² − 25. In y: y² − 4y = (y − 2)² − 4. Substituting: (x + 5)² − 25 + (y − 2)² − 4 − 7 = 0 → (x + 5)² + (y − 2)² = 36. The center is (h, k) = (−5, 2) and the radius is 6.

es: Multiplicidad PAR → toca y rebota (no cruza). Multiplicidad IMPAR → cruza el eje. Cuenta solo los factores elevados a potencia par.
en: EVEN multiplicity → touches and bounces (does not cross). ODD multiplicity → crosses the axis. Count only the factors raised to an even power.

es: g(f(3)) se lee de adentro hacia afuera: calcula f(3) primero y ese resultado entra a g. El orden importa: g(f(x)) ≠ f(g(x)).
en: g(f(3)) is read from the inside out: compute f(3) first and that result goes into g. Order matters: g(f(x)) ≠ f(g(x)).

es: 2 es el valor que sustituyes (x = 2), no el resultado de despejar k.
en: 2 is the value you substitute (x = 2), not the result of solving for k.

es: 12 no cumple p(−3) = 0. Al sustituir x = −3 queda 6 + c, y solo c = −6 lo anula.
en: 12 does not satisfy p(−3) = 0. Substituting x = −3 leaves 6 + c, and only c = −6 makes it zero.

es: (x − 3)/(x + 2) cancela el factor equivocado: se cancela (x − 3), no (x + 3). Arriba queda (x + 3).
en: (x − 3)/(x + 2) cancels the wrong factor: what cancels is (x − 3), not (x + 3). The top is left with (x + 3).

es: 11 es g(3) = 3² + 2, es decir, aplicaste solo g al 3 y olvidaste evaluar f primero.
en: 11 is g(3) = 3² + 2, that is, you applied only g to the 3 and forgot to evaluate f first.

es: 29 es f(g(3)) = 3(11) − 4, o sea invertiste el orden. g(f(3)) aplica f primero, luego g.
en: 29 is f(g(3)) = 3(11) − 4, that is, you reversed the order. g(f(3)) applies f first, then g.

es: 144π usa (1/2)πr²h. El factor del cono es 1/3, no 1/2.
en: 144π uses (1/2)πr²h. The cone factor is 1/3, not 1/2.

es: 128π = (1/3)π(8²)(6): intercambiaste radio y altura. El que va al cuadrado es el radio (6), no la altura.
en: 128π = (1/3)π(8²)(6): you swapped radius and height. The one that gets squared is the radius (6), not the height.

es: 25 = (10/2)² parte la diagonal a la mitad y la eleva al cuadrado; ese no es el lado del cuadrado.
en: 25 = (10/2)² halves the diagonal and squares it; that is not the side of the square.

es: 3/5 es sin θ = opuesto/hipotenusa = 9/15. Te piden el coseno, que usa el cateto ADYACENTE.
en: 3/5 is sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 9/15. They want the cosine, which uses the ADJACENT leg.

es: 0.4 = 1 − 0.6 treats sine and cosine as if they added to 1. What adds to 1 is sin²+cos², not sin+cos.
en: 0.4 = 1 − 0.6 treats sine and cosine as if they added to 1. What adds to 1 is sin²+cos², not sin+cos.

es: $2 es el precio de la BEBIDA (d = 2), no del hot dog. La pregunta pide h.
en: $2 is the price of the DRINK (d = 2), not the hot dog. The question asks for h.

es: La idea central abarca el giro completo. Frases como “is often described as… but ecologists describe something stranger… Increasingly, restorers aim” apuntan a la meta nueva: durar en el futuro, no rebobinar al pasado.
en: The central idea covers the whole turn. Phrases like “is often described as… but ecologists describe something stranger… Increasingly, restorers aim” point to the new goal: lasting into the future, not rewinding to the past.

es: El punto y coma ya une dos independientes; agregarle “and” es redundante (“; and” sobra).
en: The semicolon already joins two independent clauses; adding “and” is redundant (“; and” is one too many).

es: Falta la coma antes de “but”; unir dos oraciones completas sin ella es incorrecto.
en: The comma before “but” is missing; joining two complete sentences without it is wrong.

es: Completa cuadrados. En x: x² − 6x = (x − 3)² − 9. En y: y² + 8y = (y + 4)² − 16. Sustituyendo: (x − 3)² − 9 + (y + 4)² − 16 − 11 = 0 → (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 36. El centro es (h, k) = (3, −4) y el radio es 6.
en: Complete the square. In x: x² − 6x = (x − 3)² − 9. In y: y² + 8y = (y + 4)² − 16. Substituting: (x − 3)² − 9 + (y + 4)² − 16 − 11 = 0 → (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 36. The center is (h, k) = (3, −4) and the radius is 6.

es: Memoriza 30-60-90 → 1 : √3 : 2 (opuestos a 30°, 60°, 90°). El lado frente a 60° es el mediano: hipotenusa · (√3/2).
en: Memorize 30-60-90 → 1 : √3 : 2 (opposite 30°, 60°, 90°). The side facing 60° is the middle one: hypotenuse · (√3/2).

es: 1 cuenta un solo cruce, pero hay dos factores de multiplicidad impar: (x + 2)³ y (x − 4). Ambos cruzan.
en: 1 counts a single crossing, but there are two factors of odd multiplicity: (x + 2)³ and (x − 4). Both cross.

es: 11/20 es 22/40: condicionaste sobre la fila "menor de 30" en vez de la columna "negativo". El grupo dado es negativo (50).
en: 11/20 is 22/40: you conditioned on the “under 30” row instead of the “negative” column. The given group is negative (50).

es: 8/17 es sin A (opuesto/hipotenusa), no el coseno. El opuesto a A es BC = 8.
en: 8/17 is sin A (opposite/hypotenuse), not the cosine. The side opposite A is BC = 8.

es: 8/15 es tan A (opuesto/adyacente). El coseno usa la hipotenusa, no el cateto opuesto.
en: 8/15 is tan A (opposite/adjacent). The cosine uses the hypotenuse, not the opposite leg.

es: 6 es el lado opuesto a 30° (el cateto corto = hipotenusa/2), no el opuesto a 60°.
en: 6 is the side opposite 30° (the short leg = hypotenuse/2), not the one opposite 60°.

es: Falta la coma antes de “but”: cuando un FANBOYS une dos oraciones completas, esa coma es obligatoria en el SAT.
en: The comma before “but” is missing: when a FANBOYS joins two complete sentences, that comma is mandatory on the SAT.

es: El plural de family es families (con -ies); la forma “familys” no existe.
en: The plural of family is families (with -ies); the form “familys” does not exist.

es: 3x³y⁵ pone la y arriba: y⁻²/y³ = y⁻⁵, y el exponente NEGATIVO significa que y⁵ va en el denominador.
en: 3x³y⁵ puts the y on top: y⁻²/y³ = y⁻⁵, and the NEGATIVE exponent means y⁵ goes in the denominator.

es: 150π usa 1/2 en vez de 1/3. El cono es exactamente UN TERCIO del cilindro, no la mitad.
en: 150π uses 1/2 instead of 1/3. A cone is exactly ONE THIRD of the cylinder, not half.

es: Sujeto invertido: concordancia con el sujeto pospuesto
en: Inverted subject: agreement with the postponed subject

es: “Photographs were taken” deja el modificador colgando (las fotos no esperaban preservar nada) y nadie realiza “stored”.
en: “Photographs were taken” leaves the modifier dangling (the photographs were not hoping to preserve anything) and nobody performs “stored”.

es: El costo nunca se menciona; el tema es el gusto y la incomodidad, no el precio. Es un detalle que el texto no toca.
en: Cost is never mentioned; the topic is taste and discomfort, not price. It is a detail the text does not touch.

es: No la defiende de nadie; el narrador es quien la punza. “Forgave her… she thought so little” es un desprecio elegante, no una defensa.
en: It does not defend her from anyone; the narrator is the one needling her. “Forgave her… she thought so little” is an elegant put-down, not a defense.

es: −10/3 es el valor de k/3. Te detuviste un paso antes: falta multiplicar por 3.
en: −10/3 is the value of k/3. You stopped one step early: you still have to multiply by 3.

es: Iguala: x² + 6x + 12 = −3x + c → x² + 9x + (12 − c) = 0. Un solo punto → discriminante cero: 81 − 4(12 − c) = 0 → 81 − 48 + 4c = 0 → 4c = −33 → c = −33/4. Verifica: el constante queda 12 + 33/4 = 81/4 y x² + 9x + 81/4 = (x + 9/2)² = 0. ✓ En la grilla escribe -33/4 (o -8.25).
en: Set them equal: x² + 6x + 12 = −3x + c → x² + 9x + (12 − c) = 0. A single point → zero discriminant: 81 − 4(12 − c) = 0 → 81 − 48 + 4c = 0 → 4c = −33 → c = −33/4. Check: the constant becomes 12 + 33/4 = 81/4 and x² + 9x + 81/4 = (x + 9/2)² = 0. ✓ In the grid write -33/4 (or -8.25).

es: 77 sale de evaluar f(5) + 2 = 2(36) + 3 + 2: te saltaste el corrimiento x − 3 y metiste el 5 directo en f.
en: 77 comes from evaluating f(5) + 2 = 2(36) + 3 + 2: you skipped the x − 3 shift and put the 5 straight into f.

es: 167 sale de f(5 + 3) + 2 = f(8) + 2 = 2(81) + 3 + 2: sumaste el 3 en vez de restarlo. En f(x − 3), al x le RESTAS 3 antes de entrar a f.
en: 167 comes from f(5 + 3) + 2 = f(8) + 2 = 2(81) + 3 + 2: you added the 3 instead of subtracting it. In f(x − 3), you SUBTRACT 3 from x before it enters f.

es: Encadena multiplicadores: +20% → ×1.20; luego −25% → ×0.75. Efecto neto: 1.20 × 0.75 = 0.90. Si p es el precio original, 0.90p = 270 → p = 270/0.90 = 300. Verifica hacia adelante: 300 × 1.2 = 360; 360 × 0.75 = 270 ✓.
en: Chain the multipliers: +20% → ×1.20; then −25% → ×0.75. Net effect: 1.20 × 0.75 = 0.90. If p is the original price, 0.90p = 270 → p = 270/0.90 = 300. Check forward: 300 × 1.2 = 360; 360 × 0.75 = 270 ✓.

es: En probabilidad condicional, la frase “from those who…” define el DENOMINADOR. Completa siempre la tabla antes de calcular: la celda que falta casi siempre entra en la respuesta o en un distractor.
en: In conditional probability, the phrase “from those who…” defines the DENOMINATOR. Always complete the table before computing: the missing cell almost always shows up in the answer or in a distractor.

es: 1/4 = 30/120 usa el GRAN TOTAL como denominador. La frase “selected from those who travel by bus or walk” cambia el denominador a 72, no 120.
en: 1/4 = 30/120 uses the GRAND TOTAL as the denominator. The phrase “selected from those who travel by bus or walk” changes the denominator to 72, not 120.

es: Cofunctions: sin θ = cos(90° − θ). The sine of an acute angle equals the cosine of another when the two angles ADD to 90°. So (3x − 17) + (2x + 42) = 90 → 5x + 25 = 90 → 5x = 65 → x = 13. (Check: 3(13) − 17 = 22° and 2(13) + 42 = 68°; 22 + 68 = 90 ✓ and sin 22° = cos 68° ≈ 0.3746 ✓.)
en: Cofunctions: sin θ = cos(90° − θ). The sine of an acute angle equals the cosine of another when the two angles ADD to 90°. So (3x − 17) + (2x + 42) = 90 → 5x + 25 = 90 → 5x = 65 → x = 13. (Check: 3(13) − 17 = 22° and 2(13) + 42 = 68°; 22 + 68 = 90 ✓ and sin 22° = cos 68° ≈ 0.3746 ✓.)

es: 9 es el segmento largo (x + 5). La hipotenusa es la suma de ambos segmentos, no uno solo.
en: 9 is the long segment (x + 5). The hypotenuse is the sum of both segments, not just one.

es: 8/17 es sin J (o cos L), metiendo la hipotenusa 17 de la terna 8-15-17. Te pidieron tangente, que es cateto/cateto: la hipotenusa no entra.
en: 8/17 is sin J (or cos L), pulling in the hypotenuse 17 from the 8-15-17 triple. They asked for the tangent, which is leg/leg: the hypotenuse does not enter.
